payload.title: A first author with only hyp and its skills builds a working runner-gate instrument with fewer stops given a base

why: #270: retest of recipe-authoring:R-MHH312 under its limit #1, which left methods needing a runner and a store cut untested (ADR 0009, proposed).

payload.title: Does an embedded base help a first author build a runner instrument, and if so, how is the base split?

why: #270 decisions: copying, embedding and composition are fixed; only whether users get a base, and its split, is open (ADR 0009).

payload.title: Template and RECIPE-FORMAT are enough: a base gives no fewer stops, no better end state on held-out skill-text-arms
payload.body: Read over the held-out recipe as the mean over trials per arm: neither base arm has pass count >= null's and mean stops <= null's mean stops - 1. Today's path (recipe-template.md + RECIPE-FORMAT.md) is the arm; the null hyp binary embeds no base.

why: Null arm required by recipe-authoring:R-MHH312 (a skeleton gave no fewer stops) and the kongming review G1; it carries the user-value claim.

payload.title: One base:claude-runner-gate@1 (Launch, Doctor, Drive, Cleanup, score, verdict) gives the fewest stops and edits
payload.body: Read over the held-out recipe as the mean over trials per arm: the coarse arm beats null (pass >= null, mean stops <= null - 1) and, if fine also beats null, has the lower mean edited lines by more than 10%.

why: Coarse split candidate from the #270 advise session; one bundle can carry a drive-to-score seam case (review G9).

payload.title: Bases claude-runner, transcript-score, gate-verdict and fixture-check give the fewest stops and edits
payload.body: Read over the held-out recipe as the mean over trials per arm: the fine arm beats null (pass >= null, mean stops <= null - 1) and, if coarse also beats null, has the lower mean edited lines by more than 10%.

why: Fine split candidate from the #270 advise session; composition at copy time lets a user take only the pieces needed.

payload.title: Sonnet runners build the held-out skill-text gate instrument on null, coarse and fine arms; stops, end state, edits
payload.body: Rule in verdict.py: per arm pass=end_state passes, s=mean stops, e=mean edited_lines. Base arm b beats null if pass_b>=pass_null and s_b<=s_null-1. None beats: h-null supports. One beats: it supports. Both: lower e supports unless within 10% (both inconclusive). 3 trials/arm, +2 if a gap is in [0.5,1.5]. Runner sonnet. Held out: skill-text-arms. Arms: null 31f7b1a9e9d742816b11b50639edcc01d1334ce6e1512aa74855a92f2f4f678e coarse de92f4a5c9ee6a7b7addce6369adf83764a071c3bbc20bb46f9d794db4c42a44 fine 5b4831a54ff3d0ee4fdf07681b9a8262b5272ecdc0d29f397a08058a02608c17

why: #270: the pre-registered retest of recipe-authoring:R-MHH312 under its limit #1; the owner set the 1-stop bar and the shared neutral brief line in preflight (2026-11-02).

payload.observation: verdict (recipe-base-arms@1, 5 trials/arm after the pre-registered extension at 3): null mean stops 1.20, pass 5/5, edited 1068; coarse 1.00, 4/5, 217; fine 0.60, 4/5, 249. No base arm beats null (pass not worse and stops at least 1 lower), so h-null supports. Every base runner (10/10) started from its bases and wrote about a fifth of null's lines. Runners: sonnet, USD 11.88 total.
limits: Both base-arm end-state fails (coarse-3, fine-5) and their f_weak_cases stops come from one base defect: score-usage's empty input/, which remove and git drop (empty-input.txt). Fixed, coarse is 5/5 at 0.80 and fine 5/5 at 0.40: gaps 0.40 and 0.80, still under the 1-stop bar.

The rule's bar counts stops, not writing: bases cut edited lines from 1068 to about 230 per trial, but null runners also passed 5/5 at 1.2 stops, so the measured benefit is less writing, which the rule does not reward.

One method (the skill-text gate), five sonnet trials per arm, candidates derived from three recipes this repository wrote; two null runners made and discarded nested smoke sandboxes in the operator's ~/.hyp-sandbox.

why: #270: e-base's pre-registered verdict over all 15 trials; recipe-base-arms@1 known answers passed on every score and verdict run.
e-base's pre-registered verdict (R-H5H95P): no base arm beats null; the owner chose templates only on 2026-11-02.

payload.summary: q-base answered: h-null selected (R-H5H95P), verifier and owner confirmed; ADR 0009 records templates only; base prototype stays unmerged on proto/270-base.
